findings.title: `isAccessTokenId` matcher never verifies the grant shortcut (wrong offsets and inverted condition)
findings.description:
The matcher has two bugs on one line: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.
- **Wrong offsets:** the encoder writes the grant shortcut at indices 4–6 of the prefix (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:79-81`). `substring(3, 5)` takes the second token-type character plus the first grant character, e.g. `"ta"` from `onrtac`.
- **Inverted condition:** it returns `false` when the value equals the expected shortcut; the `!` is missing.

The two bugs mask each other. The extracted value always starts with `t`, so it never equals `ac`, `dg`, `rt` or `ci`, and the check never fires. `expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` (lines 145, 173, 182, 244) therefore accept any grant type. Fixing only one of the two bugs would break every caller.

A prefix shorter than 5 characters also throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of returning a mismatch. The fix is `if (items[0].length() != 6 || !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

findings.title: `rawTokenId` null check validates `grantType` a second time
findings.description: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` checks `grantType` again, so `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null raw id is accepted, and `encodeTokenId` (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:114-117`) would then emit a `jti` ending in the literal `:null`. It should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: Client-credentials and other flows never set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`, so their tokens are tagged `na`
findings.description:
The attribute is set in only five places: `TokenManager.java:248`, `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109`, `PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.java:82`, `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.java:134` and `StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237`. These flows create tokens without it:
- **Client credentials:** `ClientCredentialsGrantType` calls `responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` directly (lines 122-141) and never goes through `createTokenResponse`. Every such token gets the `na` shortcut, and the `cc` shortcut registered by `ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory` is never emitted.
- **Legacy token exchange:** `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:409-410` has the same gap.
- **UMA:** `AuthorizationTokenService.java:357-358` has the same gap.

The unit test's `trltcc:1234` case suggests coverage that the server does not provide. Either set the attribute in these flows or document that `na` is expected for them.

findings.title: `getShortcut()` contract contradicts the encoder's fixed 2-character format and is not validated
findings.description:
The Javadoc says "usually like 3-letters shortcut". Every in-repo shortcut is 2 characters, and the decoder hard-requires a 6-character prefix (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74-81`).

A factory that follows the Javadoc produces a 7-character prefix. `encodeTokenId` emits it without complaint and `getTokenContextFromTokenId` then rejects it with `IllegalArgumentException`.

`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` (lines 70-85) checks only for duplicates, not length or null. A null shortcut would throw `NullPointerException` from `ConcurrentHashMap.put` at startup. The lazy-registration paths (lines 106-137) skip even the duplicate check.

The method is also abstract with no default, so any out-of-tree `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` breaks. All nine in-repo implementations are updated. Fix the Javadoc to "exactly 2 characters" and validate at registration.

findings.title: `testIncorrectGrantType` passes because of an accidental `NullPointerException`
findings.description:
The test builds the factory with `init(null)` and never calls `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` is null. Decoding `ofrtac:5678` misses the map and dereferences `sessionFactory` at `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:125`, throwing `NullPointerException`. The `catch (RuntimeException iae)` swallows that, so the intended `IllegalArgumentException` branch (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:92-94`) is never exercised.

Further gaps in the same file:
- No test covers `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`, the only method production code calls.
- No test covers a malformed prefix length or unknown session/token shortcuts.
- `assertEquals` arguments are in (actual, expected) order throughout.

Use `Assert.assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException.class, ...)` and give the factory a stub session factory.

findings.title: Public copy constructor `Context(Context)` removed instead of extended
findings.description:
The diff deletes `public Context(Context context)` rather than adding `this.grantType = context.grantType`. No in-repo caller remains; the only construction is `TokenEndpoint.java:149`. The removal is unrelated to the feature and breaks source and binary compatibility for extensions that wrap a context. Restore it with the new field copied.

Relatedly, `grantType` is captured once from `formParams` in the constructor (line 102), and `setFormParams` (line 105) does not refresh it.

findings.title: Unused import added
findings.description: `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` is imported but never referenced in the file; line 237 uses `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE`. Remove the import.

findings.title: Inconsistent shortcut constants and overlapping shortcut values
findings.description:
Four factories expose a `GRANT_SHORTCUT` constant (authorization code, refresh, CIBA, device). The other five return inline literals (`cc`, `pg`, `pc`, `ro`, `te`).

The refresh-token shortcut `rt` is identical to `TokenType.REGULAR`'s `rt` (`AccessTokenContext.java:54`), giving IDs like `onrtrt:<uuid>`. Decoding is positional so it is unambiguous, but it is easy to misread.

Similarly, "unknown" is `un` for session and token type but `na` for grant type.

findings.title: Decoder has no production caller, and the factory's maps are loosely encapsulated
findings.description:
`getTokenContextFromTokenId` is referenced only from the unit test; production code calls only `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` and `encodeTokenId` (`TokenManager.java:1052-1054`). That is fine as groundwork, with three things to settle before it gets a caller:
- A token ID containing `:` with a non-6-character prefix throws `IllegalArgumentException` instead of being treated as legacy/unknown.
- The exception messages echo the raw token ID, which is caller-supplied.
- An unknown shortcut triggers a scan of all grant factories on every call (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:125-133`).

Separately, `grantsByShortcuts` and `grantsToShortcuts` (factory lines 41-42) are package-private, non-final and reassigned by the test to plain `HashMap`s. A package-private constructor or setter would keep the `ConcurrentHashMap` invariant.

findings.title: SPI registration and token-ID wiring are consistent
findings.description: `TokenContextEncoderSpi` is registered in `META-INF/services/org.keycloak.provider.Spi`, and the default factory is registered in its own service file. `initToken` falls back to `na` when no grant type is set, so the admin evaluation and authorization paths cannot hit the "unknown grantType" exception. `TokenEndpoint.java:114-116` guarantees non-null `formParams` before `Context` reads the grant type. The `requestedAucienceClients` → `requestedAudienceClients` rename is a correct typo fix.

`rawTokenId` null check validates `grantType` a second time
Client-credentials and other flows never set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`, so their tokens are tagged `na`
`getShortcut()` contract contradicts the encoder's fixed 2-character format and is not validated
Public copy constructor `Context(Context)` removed instead of extended
Inconsistent shortcut constants and overlapping shortcut values
Decoder has no production caller, and the factory's maps are loosely encapsulated
